note.title: Quick rules
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches Quick rules through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Quick rules.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Food and drink quantities take du/de la/de l’/des.
After ne…pas or ne…plus before a noun, use de/d’.
After aller, choose au/à la/à l’/aux from the place noun.
Movement/reflexive verbs using être may require agreement.

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Opinions.
workedExamples.answer: J’aime le riz. / Je préfère regarder la télé.
workedExamples.why: With a noun after aimer / adorer / détester / préférer, use the definite article (le / la / l’ / les). With another verb, use the infinitive without an article.

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Food & drink.
workedExamples.answer: Je bois de l’eau. / Je mange des frites.
workedExamples.why: When eating or drinking, use du / de la / de l’ / des

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Negatives.
workedExamples.answer: Je ne bois pas de coca. / Il n’y a plus de pain.
workedExamples.why: After ne…pas / ne…plus, change to de / d’

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Places after aller.
workedExamples.answer: Je vais au cinéma. / à la pharmacie. / à l’épicerie. / aux magasins.
workedExamples.why: Choose au / à la / à l’ / aux carefully

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Passé composé.

commonMistakes: Keeping du/de la after a negative.
A small article or ending can change the grammar even when the main vocabulary is recognisable.
